Subject: MAP & Eval Sprint — Dedicated GPU pool structure, pricing, and burst definition

Hi Alex,

Great talking yesterday — thanks for walking me through your 1P/2P model validation goals. Per our call, I sketched a short MAP and an evaluation sprint that should get Nova to a production-ready baseline while leaving room for a staged Dedicated reservation. High-level proposal attached (MAP-Nova-v1.pdf).

Quick summary:
- Eval sprint: 2 weeks of focused validation (SE support from Ben). Acceptance = 3 representative workloads within target latency and throughput.
- Post-acceptance ramp: if acceptance criteria met, Nova signs a staged reservation: Month 1 committed baseline (30% of target steady-state), Month 2-3 ramp to 60%, Month 4+ steady at 100% of committed GPUs.
- Pool sizing: recommended starting pool = 6 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (we can scale to 12 if the eval shows higher concurrency).
- Pricing & discounts: committed-rate per-GPU lower than on-demand. Additional tiered discounts at 6- and 12-month commits.
- Burst policy: 1.5x burst allowed up to 25% of monthly committed hours at the burst premium (35% over committed rate). Bursts beyond cap billed at on-demand. We can discuss an escrow for extra burst capacity if you need guaranteed headroom.

Attachments: MAP-Nova-v1.pdf (map), GPU-configuration-sheet.xlsx (configs). I've also included a DocuSign reservation quote link if this matches your expectations.

Ask: can procurement review the MAP and confirm whether a 6-month minimum term is acceptable? Also, do you want us to include SOC2 artifacts ahead of procurement?

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-minute walk-through with Ben (SE) and Evelyn (CS) tomorrow.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

On Alex's questions: thanks — answering inline and adding Ben & Evelyn to help with technical/onboarding details. Karthik can advise on contract term flexibility.

1) SLA: our Dedicated offering targets 99.95% availability for committed pools; for high-availability add-on we can offer 99.99% with multi-region redundancy (this is typically tacked as an enterprise SLA). We'll include the exact SLO table in the commercial quote.

2) Burst billing example (illustrative):
   - Committed: 6 GPUs x 24h x 30d = 4320 committed GPU-hours/month
   - Allowed burst: up to 25% of committed hours = 1080 GPU-hours/month at burst premium
   - Burst premium: 35% over committed per-hour rate (e.g., committed $7.00/hr -> burst $9.45/hr)
   - Example: if you use an extra 800 GPU-hours in a spike, cost = 800 * 9.45 = $7,560 additional (vs on-demand which would be ~ $12.00/hr).
   - Over-cap: any usage beyond burst cap billed at on-demand rates. We can also put an escrow arrangement for guaranteed burst headroom at a fixed monthly fee if predictability is required.

3) Pilot-to-commit path: yes — we typically structure a 3-week pilot (we can expand to 4 weeks) with credits applied as a one-time conversion credit if you convert to a committed reservation within 30 days of pilot close. For your ask, Karthik confirms we can allow a 3-month pilot converted pro-rata into a 6- or 12-month commitment with the pilot credit applied against month 1. I'll let Karthik and Legal finalize a short addendum.

4) Security: attaching SOC2 summary and the data handling checklist; Ben will also send a short onboarding checklist for dataset ingestion.

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben to run a 30-minute technical kickoff with your infra team (booked Thurs 16:30 PT).
- Monica to share a redline-ready quote via DocuSign for a 3-month pilot -> 6-month conversion path (link attached).

Monica — procurement here. A few items from legal and procurement to keep the commercial review moving: 

- We prefer a 3-month pilot but require an explicit conversion mechanism to longer terms with clear SKU-level pricing. Please provide a redlineable contract and a DocuSign envelope.
- SLA: 99.9% is acceptable; for the pilot we accept 99.5% with defined credits for downtime. For conversion, we want the 99.9% SLO in contract.
- Burst cap: please include a clause that burst beyond 25% will not automatically scale on our behalf; any additional burst above cap must be initiated by a signed change order or pre-approved form.
- Data retention & audit logs: provide the retention table and access options for audit logs (we need 12-month access for internal audits).

Please supply the requested contract doc and the SOC2 artifact links. We'll target an internal procurement decision the week of Jul 5 if we get the redlines this week.
